description:
## Why

Currently `pkix-path::DefaultVerifier` supports only two algorithms:
* RSA-PKCS1v15 + SHA-256 (`1.2.840.113549.1.1.11`)
* ECDSA P-256 + SHA-256 (`1.2.840.10045.4.3.2`)

Real-world chains routinely use other algorithms. PKITS doesn't exercise this much because it's RFC-conformance focused, but a TLS chain in 2026 typically uses one of:

* **RSA-PSS** (`1.2.840.113549.1.1.10`) — preferred in TLS 1.3, used by many modern CAs
* **ECDSA P-384** (`1.2.840.10045.4.3.3`) — common in modern TLS, code signing, sigstore
* **Ed25519** (`1.3.101.112`) — modern TLS, increasingly common

Without these, downstream consumers hitting these algorithms see `AlgorithmNotAllowed` (or worse, the OID dispatcher in `DefaultVerifier` returns `signature::Error::new()` with no useful info). The differential test harness will surface this loudly as `StricterThanWild` once we add a corpus that includes modern chains.

## What

Five new `SignatureVerifier` impl unit-structs in `pkix-path/src/lib.rs`, one per algorithm, each behind its own feature flag. `DefaultVerifier` (`lib.rs:3047`) gains OID dispatch entries for each. Each algorithm reuses the existing RustCrypto crate already in the dependency graph or pulls in a sibling crate (`p384`, `p521`, `ed25519-dalek` etc).

Pattern is established by the existing `EcdsaP256Verifier` (`lib.rs:1867`) and `RsaPkcs1v15Sha256Verifier` (`lib.rs:1909`) — copy and adapt per algorithm.

## Recommended decomposition (file children when work starts)

1. **RSA-PSS-SHA256 verifier** (P2) — most-impactful single algorithm. Note: PSS has algorithm parameters (saltLength, mgf1HashAlgorithm) that must be parsed from `AlgorithmIdentifier`. There are multiple 'valid' PSS encodings in the wild — this is itself a divergence class the harness should surface.
2. **ECDSA P-384 + SHA-384 verifier** (P2) — `p384` crate exists in RustCrypto.
3. **Ed25519 verifier** (P2) — `ed25519-dalek` or `ed25519` crate.
4. **RSA-PKCS1v15 SHA-384 + SHA-512** (P3) — extends existing RSA verifier with two more OIDs.
5. **ECDSA P-521 + SHA-512** (P3) — `p521` crate.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each algorithm has its own `SignatureVerifier` impl, feature flag, and unit tests using independent oracles (RustCrypto test vectors, RFC 4231/8032 test vectors, NIST CAVS).
- [ ] `DefaultVerifier` dispatches to all enabled verifiers via OID match.
- [ ] No new test uses `pkix-path` itself as the oracle — every test verifies against a known-correct independently-computed signature.
- [ ] `pkix-difftest run pkits ...` baseline unchanged (PKITS doesn't exercise these algos, so all chains stay in their current buckets).
- [ ] A new sample chain (real-world cert with one of these algos) added to `pkix-difftest/tests/fixtures/` and exercised by the existing smoke tests.
- [ ] No `unsafe`. No new top-level workspace deps that pull in C/C++.
- [ ] `pkix-path` stays `no_std` — every new verifier opt-in via feature flag and the underlying crate is no_std-capable.

## Out of scope

- ML-DSA / Dilithium (covered by `pkix-composite` follow-up).
- DSA (deprecated; not implementing).
- ECDSA over non-NIST curves (secp256k1, brainpool).
- RSA-PSS-SHA384, RSA-PSS-SHA512 (file as a follow-up if needed; PSS-SHA256 covers the bulk of real-world use).

## Filed as

v1.0 'bar' item per gap audit: `pkix-path` crypto coverage. Estimated ~200 lines of new code total + tests, spread across 5 children. Each child is roughly half a day of focused work.
title: pkix-path: signature algorithm coverage (RSA-PSS, P-384, Ed25519, P-521, RSA-SHA384/512)
